text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will today visit the industrial sites of Shanghai. Egypt and Singapore sign an agreement to set up a commercial port and a free zone.
- U.S. President Clinton discusses with Middle East envoy Dennis Ross America's next step and says that the current crisis facing the Israeli government is an internal matter.

- Official source at the finance ministry says education, healthcare and subsidies are the goverment's priorities in the 85 billion pound ($25 billion) 1997/8 budget. State to spend 24.6 billion pounds on wages and pensions, 18 billion on education, healthcare and basic services.

- State's Holding Company for Rice and Flour Mills decided at its annual general meeting to privatise 16 rice mills, five animal feed factories and six macaroni factories. Company also decided to refurbish 60 other mills with a total investment of 600 million pounds over three years.
- Ganzouri says after speaking to Chinese officials: Egypt is the first Arab economic "tiger" in the region. We have made important developments in investment and in the economy.
- Egyptian cotton exporters association is optimistic about sales after Ganzouri's visit to South East Asia and China.
- Parliament to begin its discussion of the 1997/8 budget on Thursday.
